extracted.intended_audience: editors, proofreaders, compositors, authors, and typesetters (particularly at academic/University presses)
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive typographical and copy-editing style manual (University of Chicago Press) giving rules and examples for composition, capitalization, italics, quotations, punctuation, divisions, footnotes, indexing, tabular work, technical terms, and proofreader practice for printed books and periodicals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for Composition
rubrics_metrics.description: General principles governing composition and application of typographical rules in the Press's publications; rules are meant for the average case and applied with elasticity; exceptions are permitted where subject-matter or author preference justifies deviation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains scope and purpose of the Manual: not absolute law, allows discretion for exceptions, recognizes local and subject-matter differences; emphasizes applicability in the printing-office, common-sense over abstract logic, and deference to authors where taste/logic not involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed numbered rules specifying when to capitalize words in English (proper nouns, epithets, particles in foreign names, geographical names, political divisions, thoroughfares, party names, titles, biblical terms, first words of sentences, titles of publications, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains many specific rules and counterexamples (e.g., capitalize proper nouns and adjectives derived from them; do not capitalize verbs derived from proper names — to boycott; capitalize the first word of a sentence and of quoted direct speech; capitalize principal words in English titles; rules for foreign-language titles; rules for academic and institutional names; guidance for capitalization after colons, in enumerations, ordinals, scientific names, feast-days, and more). Numerous examples and noted exceptions accompany almost every item.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Use of Italics
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules indicating which words or phrases should be set in italics (emphasis, foreign words not incorporated into English, brief foreign sentences, certain names of works or technical terms where italics are preferred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives examples (emphasis: 'This was, however, not the case'; foreign words: coup d'etat, par excellence) and lists exceptions (do not italicize foreign titles preceding names or foreign institution/place names that have English function; do not italicize anglicized foreign words such as entree, per cent). Also cross-references to sections on reduced type for longer foreign passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for handling quotations in the text: punctuation, capitalization of first words, shorter vs longer quotations, and integration with surrounding text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules on capitalization of the first word of a quotation when it starts a sentence or when connected with the preceding clause; when to set quotations in reduced type or as block quotations (see related sections); examples showing punctuation placement and use of quotation marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on spelling choices and a list of words whose spelling offers a choice of practice; approach favors progressive conservatism and uniformity where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes preferred spellings for variable words and indicates where the Press accepts alternative forms; accounts for learned-society conventions and evolving literary practice; intended to produce practical uniformity across publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules for punctuation usage in printed material, including commas, semicolons, colons, periods, quotation punctuation, parentheses, dashes, and special cases (e.g., punctuation with quotations, enumerations, and headings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides numbered rules and examples, notes on exceptions, and interactions with capitalization rules (e.g., capitalization after colons only in certain circumstances). Emphasizes clarity and printing-office applicability; cross-references related items (e.g., quotations, capitalization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisions (Heads and Sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for dividing text into chapters, sections, paragraphs, and for setting headings and subheadings (including capitalization, typography, and placement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises on use of cap-and-small-cap, italic side-heads, center-heads, bold-face cut-in heads; cautions that some typographic forms (e.g., cap-and-small-cap and italics for center-heads) should be avoided when possible; gives rules for capitalization in heads and box-heads in tables (see 279–82).

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for the composition, punctuation, numbering, and formatting of footnotes and notes (including when to use notes rather than running text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies numbering conventions, note punctuation (e.g., 'Note.—' with period and dash), placement, and examples of citations in footnotes and bibliographies (the second edition expanded the method of citing references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and recommendations for compiling indexes: entry formation, capitalization, order, and special treatments for names and technical terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes summarization of rules (added/expanded in second edition), guidance intended for librarians and indexers, and cross-references to related sections (spelling, foreign names, scientific names).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for preparing tables: layout, heads, use of cap-and-small-cap in box-heads, numeric alignment, and typographic conventions for tabular data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refers to specific rules for cap-and-small-cap box-heads (see 279–82), recommends avoiding certain heading styles in narrow measure, and provides examples of table formatting to ensure clarity and consistency in printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for handling scientific, botanical, zoological, geological, and other technical terms, including capitalization conventions for Latin names and species epithets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives rules such as: capitalize scientific Latin names of divisions/orders/genera; capitalize species names only when derived from proper names (botanical/zoological), but not in geological or medical contexts; includes many examples (Vertebrata, Reptilia, Rosa Carolina, Pterygomatopus schmidti) and cross-references to spelling and punctuation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix (Supplementary Rules and Examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material including extended examples, lists (e.g., words with variant spellings), and additional clarifying rules that expand on core sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to collect exceptions, extended lists, and explanatory material not placed in the main rule sequence; examples are placed after each division of rules to aid clarity (a change in second edition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hints to Authors and Editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical advice for authors and editors preparing manuscripts for the Press: submission conventions, preferred manuscript preparation, and common pitfalls to avoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides editorial guidance designed to reduce typesetting problems and to conform incoming work to the Press's typographical practices; covers matters such as citation form, manuscript layout, and preferred stylistic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hints to Proofreaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for proofreaders on how to apply the Manual's rules, exercise discretion, and handle exceptions in proofreading work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the Manual's origins as guidance for proofreaders, notes on flexibility and deference to authorial preference, and specific proofreading expectations and marks (see Proofreader's Marks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hints to Copyholders and Proofreader's Marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical rules for copyholders (the person following the compositor's proof) and a catalog of proofreader's marks to be used in corrections and communication with compositors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains a standardized set of proofreading marks and instructions for their use; provides examples and a glossary of symbols to ensure consistent corrections and communication in the manufacturing department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens of Types in Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimen pages showing typefaces, point sizes, and examples of how text appears in various fonts and sizes used by the Press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large collection of type specimens (many faces and sizes, with sample lines and numerals) intended to guide selection of type, to show visual effects of different faces/sizes, and to serve as reference for compositors and designers.
